harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: On node1, created datauser and enforced a 100MB filesystem-level quota on /srv/data using an XFS loop-mounted filesystem (ext4 quota kernel modules unavailable), verified enforcement, and completed the mandatory single-node restart/recovery protocol with boot-identity proof.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 OS/kernel/filesystem to determine quota capability (Ubuntu 16.04, kernel 4.4.0-210-generic, root ext4 with missing quota_v2/quota_tree modules)
Installed quota, quotatool, xfsprogs packages
Created 512MB sparse backing image /var/lib/srvdata.img, formatted XFS, added persistent /etc/fstab entry with uquota option, mounted at /srv/data
Created system user datauser
Set 100MB (bsoft=100m,bhard=100m) XFS user quota for datauser on /srv/data via xfs_quota
Verified enforcement: writes succeeded up to 100MB, next write failed with Disk quota exceeded
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id, quota state, mount status
Rebooted node1 via sudo reboot, confirmed disconnect, polled until reachable again
Verified boot_id changed confirming real restart
Re-verified /srv/data mount recovery, quota configuration persistence, datauser existence, and re-ran the write-enforcement test post-restart, then cleaned up test files

evidence.requirement: Filesystem-enforced 100MB quota for datauser on /srv/data configured
evidence.summary: xfs_quota limit command set bsoft=100m,bhard=100m for datauser; report confirms 100M soft/hard limits on /srv/data

evidence.requirement: Quota enforcement demonstrated at the filesystem level
evidence.summary: datauser wrote 60MB successfully, then a second 60MB write failed with 'Disk quota exceeded' after reaching exactly 100M used, confirmed via xfs_quota report and df
Captured boot_id 6ab98831-2739-47d3-b99c-0784ebb8b49e, quota reset to 0/100M, and confirmed srv-data.mount active
sudo reboot issued in background; SSH connection closed by remote host confirming reboot command executed

evidence.requirement: Node1 boot identity changed proving actual restart
evidence.summary: Immediately after reboot, SSH connection refused (node down); subsequent poll succeeded with new boot_id 10f9f6da-4eeb-4e52-b624-e33085c73ac7, differing from pre-restart value, and new uptime -s timestamp

After restart, /srv/data automounted via srv-data.mount, xfs_quota report still shows 100M limit for datauser, datauser account intact, and write-enforcement test repeated successfully (60MB ok, next write hit Disk quota exceeded at 100M), then cleaned up leaving quota at 0 used

attempts.summary: On node1, created datauser and enforced a 100MB filesystem-level quota on /srv/data using an XFS loop-mounted filesystem (ext4 quota kernel modules unavailable), verified enforcement, and completed the mandatory single-node restart/recovery protocol with boot-identity proof.
